notes: Written as worship, not description: by people who believe Jesus Christ is Lord and Savior, for guests standing in your home.
He and His are capitalized for Jesus throughout, out of reverence.
Verses are the free Berean Standard Bible for now. Once you have your licenses, choose NIV, ESV or NLT per verse and paste the text in; I'll set up a page for that.
Every verse was checked by script against its source text.
Nothing is final. Every line stays marked draft until you approve it.

subjects.title: Jesus Christ
subjects.short: The Son of God, hungry after forty days, rests His head in His hand.

more.story: He chose this weakness for us. He knows hunger and weariness from the inside, and He did not turn from either.

verses.text: Surely He took up our infirmities and carried our sorrows
we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.

subjects.title: The Angels
subjects.short: Angels come from heaven to serve the Lord in His hunger.

more.story: Satan tempted Him with the promise of angels. He refused to test His Father, and the angels came anyway, as servants to their King.

verses.text: For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.

subjects.title: The Basilisk
subjects.short: A small winged serpent lies low near Him. It may be a basilisk.

more.story: Moretto’s Bible promised that the faithful would tread on the basilisk. In Christ that promise is kept, and the serpent’s power over us is broken.

verses.text: Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.
I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions

subjects.note: Psalm 90:13 is the Latin Bible’s numbering (91:13 in modern Bibles). The Met does not name the creature, so the short line says “may be”.

subjects.title: The Lion
subjects.short: The lion, king of beasts, lies at the feet of the King of kings.

more.story: Daniel needed an angel to shut the lions’ mouths. This lion needs no angel. It knows its Lord and lies down.

verses.text: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions.
Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed

subjects.title: The Stag
subjects.short: A stag bends toward Him, its head lowered.

more.story: The psalmist longed for God as a deer longs for water. Here that longing has found Him. Whoever is thirsty may come.

verses.text: As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul longs after You, O God.
If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.

subjects.title: The Fox
subjects.short: A fox rests a few steps from Him.

more.story: Every creature on this hillside has a place to sleep. Their Maker had nowhere to lay His head, and He bore it for us.

verses.text: Through Him all things were made
Foxes have dens… but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.

subjects.title: The Bear
subjects.short: A bear lies in the grass with its head bowed.

more.story: A man alone in these hills should fear a bear. With Jesus Christ, the wild is at peace, as Isaiah said it would be.

verses.text: The cow will graze with the bear, their young will lie down together
He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.

subjects.title: The Missing Picture
subjects.short: Faint cherubs at the left edge, where the original canvas was cut away.

more.story: This was once part of a larger painting of His life. His story continues past the frame, to the cross and the empty tomb.

verses.text: There are many more things that Jesus did.

subjects.title: The Pelican
subjects.short: A white bird bends low beside Him.

more.story: Christians once believed the pelican fed its young with its own blood. It became a picture of Christ, who gave His life for us.

verses.text: I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness
Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.

subjects.note: In the Latin Bible Moretto knew, Psalm 101:7 (102:6 today) names “a pelican of the wilderness”. This is the white bird beside His head; tell me if you meant another.

subjects.title: The Serpent at His Feet
subjects.short: A thin serpent slips beneath His bare foot.

more.story: God promised in Eden that the serpent would strike the heel and have its head crushed. Here the heel rests above it, unafraid.

verses.text: He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet.

subjects.title: The Tree
subjects.short: A tree rises over Him, green and red against the sky.

more.story: Adam lost the tree of life in Eden. One day Jesus Christ would carry our sins on a tree, to open the way back.

verses.text: In the middle of the garden were the tree of life
He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree

beats.title: In the Beginning
beats.short: God made us to rule over His creation, at peace with every living thing.

more.story: When we turned from God, that peace was lost. The wild became something to fear.

verses.text: Rule over… every creature that crawls upon the earth.

beats.title: The Promise
beats.short: Even as sin entered the world, God promised a Savior.

more.story: A son of Eve would crush the serpent’s head. That son is Jesus Christ, born of a woman for us.

verses.text: He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.
But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman

beats.title: Forty Years
beats.short: God led His people through the wilderness for forty years.

more.story: He fed them every morning, and still they doubted Him. We are not so different.

verses.text: Remember that these forty years the LORD your God led you all the way in the wilderness

beats.title: Forty Days
beats.short: Jesus Christ walks into the same wilderness and goes without food for forty days.

more.story: Where Israel failed, and where we fail, He stood firm. Each time He answered the tempter with the word of God.

verses.text: Man does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.

beats.title: Fully Man
beats.short: He felt hunger and weariness as we do.

more.story: God made man a little lower than the angels. The Son of God came down to that place to lift us up.

verses.text: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.
But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor

beats.title: The Angels
beats.short: Satan offered Him angels as a test.

more.story: He would not test His Father. When the temptations ended, the angels came to serve Him.

verses.text: For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.

beats.title: Lord of the Wild
beats.short: Satan quoted Psalm 91 to Him, and stopped just before the verse about the lion.

more.story: Here the lion and the serpent already lie at His feet. The psalm Satan left unfinished is fulfilled in Him.

verses.text: You will tread on the lion and cobra; you will trample the young lion and serpent.
I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions

beats.note: Satan quotes Psalm 91:11–12 in Matthew 4:6; verse 13 is the next line.

beats.title: That You May Believe
beats.short: Moretto painted the Son of God hungry, and the wild beasts bowing to Him.

more.story: Both are true. He became one of us, so that we could belong to Him forever.

verses.text: These are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God
